candidates.core_provocation: In a workplace where employees can exchange memories to cover one another’s shifts, an exhausted worker swaps a day of memory with a new colleague. The next morning, both remember the same murder—but each remembers the other holding the weapon.
candidates.why_interesting: The exchange creates an immediate mystery in which both characters may be witnesses, victims, or killers.

candidates.core_provocation: In a company where memories can be sold, an employee trades away her last memory of her late sister to save a coworker’s job. When the coworker claims that memory proves she caused a fatal workplace accident, she must decide whether to recover the truth or protect the person who bought it.
candidates.why_interesting: It turns a deeply personal memory into evidence, property, and a possible weapon.

candidates.core_provocation: A company requires every departing employee to exchange one memory with their replacement so that workplace knowledge will survive. On her last day, a woman receives a memory from the company’s founder, who officially disappeared years ago—and in it, someone is preparing to erase her next.
candidates.why_interesting: A simple workplace handover becomes a tense discovery about who controls the organization’s collective memory.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first candidate has the clearest immediate hook and the strongest tension: two coworkers share an impossible crime scene while accusing each other through their own memories. It also keeps the cast, setting, and timeline small enough for an exciting short story.
